claim: says a no-effect sigil can mean the target was protected from the sigil strike
rule: If the healer saves the sigil target the Sigilist is told so; no effect covers only a target who did not attack or an attacker protected by night immunity (plus an attack made through a body, which a sigil cannot punish)

claim: says a no-effect result can mean an attacker was protected
rule: A healer save of the sigil target is reported to the Sigilist as a save; no effect means only no attack or a night-immune attacker

claim: claims a spent sigil that did not trigger clears the target of attacking that night
rule: No effect also fits an attacker protected by night immunity (Serial Killer), so it does not clear anyone

claim: treats a player who survived a wolf attack with no save announced as publicly looking immune
rule: An attack on a player who cannot be killed at night is never announced, so nobody can see a survived attack with no save unless a player claims it

claim: says to spend a self-bet every night once two points are banked
rule: Fortune Teller may bet on itself only up to twice per game

claim: says a blocked-player report gives the village firm evidence that a Chanteuse is alive
rule: A self-reported block is an unverified claim, and a Necromancer using a dead Chanteuse body can also block

claim: suggests picking a claimed role that bypasses protection
rule: The healer protects against any night attack; no role bypasses protection (only night-immune targets cannot be killed)
